Kugawana · Admin console

Running Kugawana from the console

Everything an administrator does day to day: reviewing the food people share, moving it through the warehouse, releasing it to the community, and keeping points, members and support in order.

Audience
Country admins & super admins
Console address
/console
Screens covered
33

Start here

What this covers

The Kugawana admin console is the web back office for the platform. Members share and request food in the mobile app; administrators use the console to check what has been offered, decide what is safe to release, move it through storage, and hand it out.

This guide walks through every screen in the order the sidebar presents them. Each section says what the screen is for, what you can do on it, and what happens to members when you act. Screenshots are taken from a working system with sample data.

A note on the screenshots

All names, phone numbers and listings shown here belong to a demonstration database. Nothing in this guide contains real member data.

Start here

The two admin roles

Every console account is one of two kinds, and the difference decides both what you see in the sidebar and how much of the data you can reach.

Country admin

Runs a single country. Everything is filtered to that country automatically — the donations list, orders, members, top-up requests, warehouses and reports all show that country only. The country name appears in the top-right of every page, and the filtering cannot be switched off or worked around.

Super admin

Runs the whole network. Sees every country's data at once — the top-right shows Global instead of a country name — and gets an extra Platform group in the sidebar for countries, admin accounts and system settings.

Why this matters

A country admin cannot see, edit or act on anything belonging to another country, even by editing a web address. Attempting it returns a "forbidden" page rather than the record.

Start here

Signing in

Go to /console and you will land on the sign-in page. Only administrator accounts can get in here — a donor or receiver who tries their app password will be turned away.

  1. Enter the email address your account was created with.
  2. Enter your password. Use Show to check it if you are unsure.
  3. Choose Sign in. You land on the dashboard.

If you cannot get in

  • "These credentials do not match our records" — the email or password is wrong. Use Forgot password.
  • "This account does not have admin access" — the password was right, but the account is either a member account or has been suspended. A super admin can re-activate it under Admins.
  • "Verify your email to continue" — email verification for admins is switched on and your address has not been confirmed. A fresh link is sent automatically each time you try; open it and sign in again.
  • Too many attempts — sign-in is limited to ten tries a minute per address. Wait a minute and try again.

Resetting a password

Enter your address and a reset link is emailed to you. The link is single-use and expires. If nothing arrives, the platform's email server may not be set up yet — see Settings.

Start here

Getting around

Every page shares the same frame: a grouped sidebar on the left, and a header strip across the top.

The sidebar

Grouped by the kind of work rather than alphabetically — Operations for the daily flow of food, Catalog for the lists that feed the app's pickers, Community for people and posts, then Growth, Insights, Support and (for super admins) Platform. The panel icon beside the page title collapses the sidebar to icons, and the console remembers your choice on that browser.

Reported problems carries a number badge when unhandled reports are waiting.

The header

  • Search — searches food listings by title or donor name, wherever you are.
  • Country tag — the country you are scoped to, or Global for super admins.
  • Bell — turns on browser alerts so you are notified of new activity even when the console is not open. Your browser will ask permission the first time.
  • Your name and role — sign out from the bottom of the sidebar.

One convention worth knowing

Across the console, the status pill is the switch. Where a list shows Active, Enabled or Published, clicking that pill flips it to the opposite state. There is no separate "deactivate" button to hunt for — this holds for warehouses, categories, FAQs, policy pages, point bundles and countries alike.

Overview · Dashboard

Dashboard

The landing page after sign-in, and the fastest way to see whether anything needs you today.

The six figures

FigureWhat it counts
Food listingsEvery listing ever created in your scope, whatever its status.
Meals distributedOrders that reached completion — food actually handed over.
Active usersDonors and receivers who have not been suspended. Admin accounts are excluded.
RevenueThe money value of approved point top-ups.
Points issuedEvery point ever credited — purchases, rewards and refunds together.
Pending reviewListings sitting at Pending or Reviewed. Your queue.

Below the figures

  • Donations this week — listings created per day over the last seven days, busiest day highlighted.
  • Recent activity — the five newest events across listings, top-up requests and orders.
  • Awaiting review — the six oldest listings still waiting on a decision. Click any row to open it.

Operations · Food donations

Food donations

The register of every piece of food offered to the platform. This is where most of the day's work happens.

Finding a listing

  • Status tabs — All, Pending, Reviewed, Approved, Published and Expired. Start on Pending each morning.
  • Search — the header search box matches the food's title or the donor's name.
  • The list is newest first, twenty-five to a page.

What the columns tell you

Each row carries the reference (FD-7), the food, who offered it, its category, the quantity, whether it is Whole or has been split into units, the district it is collected from, how long it has been waiting, and its current status.

Exporting

Export CSV downloads every listing in your scope as a spreadsheet — reference, title, donor, category, quantity, unit size, units left, district, status, points, expiry and submission date. Useful for reporting to partners.

Operations · Food donations · Detail

Reviewing a listing

Click any row to open it. This screen is where a listing is judged, priced and moved along.

The lifecycle

Food moves through six stages. The panel on the right shows where this listing has reached.

  1. Pending — just submitted by a member. Nobody has looked at it.
  2. Reviewed — an admin has seen it but not yet decided.
  3. Approved — accepted onto the platform and priced, but not yet visible to members.
  4. Collected — picked up from the donor.
  5. Stored — booked into a warehouse.
  6. Published — live in the app. Members can now request it.

Two further outcomes sit outside that line: Rejected for food that will not be accepted, and Expired for food that ran out of time.

Checking before you decide

The page gives you the photographs, the description, the pickup address and contact number, when the food was prepared, when it expires, any special instructions, and the donor with their responsibility score. Contact donor reaches them if something needs clarifying.

Approving

  1. Set Points required — what a member spends to claim this food.
  2. Optionally choose the warehouse it will be stored in.
  3. Choose Approve. You return to the register with the listing marked Approved.

Rejecting

Choose Reject and add a note explaining why. The note stays on the record.

Publishing

Publish makes the listing visible in the app. Points must be above zero first — publishing a listing priced at nothing is refused with "Assign points before publishing".

Moving through the warehouse

Once approved, mark the listing Collected when it leaves the donor and Stored when it is booked in.

Correcting a listing

Edit food opens every field the donor filled in — title, description, category, quantity and unit, dates, pickup address, contact, instructions, warehouse, points and location. You can untick photographs to delete them and upload replacements, up to five images (JPEG, PNG or WebP, 5 MB each). The food stays credited to the original donor.

One restriction

If the listing has already been split into units, its total quantity is locked. Undo the split first.

Operations · Food donations · Detail

Splitting food into units

A 10 kg sack of rice should not have to go to one household or go to waste. Splitting breaks a bulk donation into portions that several families can each claim.

How to split

  1. Open the listing and find Consumable units on the right.
  2. Enter the unit size — the portion one household receives. It cannot exceed the total.
  3. Enter points per unit — the price of a single portion, not the whole batch.
  4. Set Credit the food to. Usually the original donor. If the food came from an agency with no account, open The donor is not in the system yet and type their name, phone and email — a credit-only record is created that nobody can sign into.
  5. Choose Split into units.

The register then shows units remaining against the total instead of Whole, and members claim one portion at a time.

Undoing a split

Undo split returns the listing to a single item — but only while no units have been claimed. Once a member has taken a portion the split is permanent, and you will see "Units have already been claimed, so this split cannot be undone".

Operations · Food donations · Add food

Adding food yourself

Not all food arrives through the app. Agencies, NGOs and walk-in donors hand over stock without ever creating an account. Add food records it directly.

  1. Fill in the food: title, description, category, quantity and unit.
  2. Set the expiry date — it must be in the future. A preparation date, if given, cannot be in the future.
  3. Add pickup address, contact number and any special instructions.
  4. Choose the warehouse, if it is going into storage.
  5. Set points required.
  6. Say where it came from: pick an existing member, or type the agency's name, phone and email to create a credit-only record.
  7. Upload up to five photographs.
  8. Finish with Approve to hold it back, or Publish to put it live immediately. Publishing needs points above zero.
Country admins

The country is fixed to yours and the warehouse list only offers your own active warehouses.

Operations · Orders

Orders

Every request a member has made for food. Your job here is to accept them, mark them handed over, and cancel the ones that fall through.

Single requests and baskets

A member who requests one item produces a single order, referenced OR-1. A member who checks out several items at once produces a basket, referenced BSK- followed by six characters. Baskets are shown as one card with each item on its own line, so you can act on the whole basket or on individual items.

A basket whose items are in different states is labelled Mixed.

The three actions

ActionAvailable whenWhat happens
AcceptPendingOrder becomes Accepted and the member is notified their request was accepted.
DeliverPending or acceptedOrder becomes Completed, the handover is timestamped, and the member is told it was delivered.
CancelPending or acceptedOrder becomes Cancelled, the member's points are refunded, and the food goes back on the shelf.

Cancelling and refunds

Cancelling is not just a status change. The points the member spent are returned to their balance as an "order refund", the stock is released back to the listing, and if the listing had sold out it is republished so others can claim it. Cancel a basket and every eligible line is refunded individually.

If an action does not take

Should someone else act on the same order first, you will see a message such as "Order 4 is no longer pending" rather than the action going through twice. Refresh the page to see the current state. This is deliberate — it stops an order being refunded twice.

Operations · Warehouses

Warehouses

The storage sites food can be booked into. Each warehouse shows how many donations are held against it.

Adding or editing

A warehouse needs a name and a country. You can also record the district, street address, map coordinates, whether it has cold storage, its capacity, and free-text notes. The list shows all of this at a glance, along with how many food items are held there.

Taking one out of use

Warehouses are never deleted — deleting one would break the history of every donation stored there. Click the Active pill instead and the site becomes Inactive: past records stay intact, and it stops being offered when you approve or add food.

Country admins

You see and manage your own country's warehouses only, and new ones are created in your country regardless of what the form is set to.

Operations · Points

Points

Points are the currency members spend to claim food. This screen handles both sides: the bundles they can buy, and the requests waiting on your approval.

Point bundles

New bundle creates a points-for-money pack. Each bundle has a name, a number of points, a price and a currency. Existing bundles can be edited, disabled — hidden from members while staying on past records — or deleted outright.

Country admins see their own country's bundles plus any global ones. Disabled bundles remain visible here so you can bring them back.

Top-up requests

When a member buys points, the request lands here showing who asked, how many points, the amount, and the payment method.

  • Approve — credits the points to their balance immediately.
  • Reject — declines it; no points are credited.

Each request can only be settled once. If it has already been handled you will see "This request was already processed".

Catalog · Categories

Categories

The food types members choose from when they create a listing — vegetables, fruits, bakery, dry foods and so on.

Type a name and add it; the name must be unique. Categories are enabled or disabled rather than deleted — click the Enabled pill to turn one off. A disabled category stops being offered to members while existing listings keep their label. The count beside each one shows how much it is used.

Catalog · Learn

Learn

Educational articles shown in the app's Learn section — how to keep food safely, how to waste less, how to eat well.

An article needs a title, a category and a body. You can add a cover image (JPEG, PNG or WebP, up to 5 MB). The five categories are Food preservation, Nutrition, Safe handling, Reducing waste and Community guides.

Community · Community

Community posts

What members post to each other in the app. This screen is for moderation.

Each post shows who wrote it, when, what it says, and how many likes and comments it has attracted. Which button you get depends on the post's current state:

  • A Published post offers Remove, which takes it out of the app's feed. You are asked to confirm first.
  • A Hidden post offers Restore, which puts it back.

Removing never destroys a post, so any moderation decision can be reversed. Country admins only see posts written by members of their own country.

Community · Members

Members

Everyone using the app — donors and receivers. Admin accounts are not listed here; they live under Admins.

A member's page

Opening a member shows the food they have shared, the food they have requested, their points balance and full points history, and their responsibility score — a standing figure that reflects how reliably they have behaved.

Granting points

Enter an amount and a reason, then Grant points. The credit appears in their history against the reason you gave, so grants stay auditable. To reward several people at once, select them on the register and use the bulk grant.

Submitting the same grant twice in quick succession is caught and skipped, so a double-click will not pay twice.

Suspending

Suspend member blocks the account from the app. The same button reactivates them.

Growth · Reward campaigns

Reward campaigns

Standing rules that hand out points automatically, used to encourage people to join and to share food.

Setting one up

A campaign needs a name, a number of points and a type:

  • Signup — credited once when a new member finishes registering.
  • Donation — credited when a member shares food.
  • Manual — not automatic; a record of a reward you hand out yourself.

You can add a description, restrict it to one country, and give it a start and end date. The end date cannot fall before the start.

Campaigns can be switched off with End and switched back on later, or deleted permanently.

Insights · Reports

Reports

The longer view, for board meetings and partner reporting.

  • Total donations, orders completed, points spent and reward points issued.
  • A six-month bar chart of listings per month.
  • Top donors — the five members who have shared most, with how many ratings they have received and their average star rating.
  • Top receivers — the five members who have requested most.

For a row-by-row export, use Export CSV on the donations register.

Support · FAQs

FAQs

The questions and answers members read in the app's help section.

Each entry is a question, an answer and a sort order — lower numbers appear first. Click the Published pill to hide an entry; it stays here as Hidden for you to bring back. Delete removes it for good.

Support · Policy pages

Policy pages

Longer documents the app links to — terms of service, privacy policy, community guidelines.

A page has a title, a web address ending (its slug, which must be unique), a body of up to 50,000 characters, and a sort order. The Published pill takes a page down without losing the text; Delete removes it permanently.

Take care with the slug

The app links to policy pages by their slug. Changing it on a live page breaks any existing link to that document.

Support · Contact details

Contact details

How members reach your team. These details appear on the app's help screen.

Set a short introduction, an email address, a phone number, a WhatsApp number and your opening hours. Every field is optional — leave one blank and it simply does not appear in the app.

Support · Reported problems

Reported problems

Problems members have reported from the app. The sidebar shows a badge with the number still unhandled.

Working the queue

Open a report to read it in full, along with the reporter's name, email and phone so you can reach them directly. Set the status and record what was done in Internal notes, then Save.

Notes are private

Internal notes are only ever shown in the console. To actually reply to the member, contact them using the email or phone shown on the report.

Reports move through four states:

  • New — nobody has picked it up. These are what the sidebar badge counts.
  • In progress — being looked into.
  • Resolved — dealt with, and the time recorded.
  • Closed — finished with, whether or not it was fixed.

The admin who handled each report is recorded against it. Country admins only see reports from their own country's members.

Platform · Countries Super admin

Countries

Every country in the world is listed here; you enable the ones Kugawana actually operates in. The line at the top keeps the running count — "1 of 196 countries enabled".

Each card shows the country, its currency and how many members it has. Use the search box to find one rather than scrolling. Enable switches a country on; enabled countries show Enabled and can be switched back off.

Countries are what everything else is grouped by — members, admins, warehouses, campaigns and food all belong to one. Disabling a country removes it from every picker in the console while leaving existing records untouched.

Enable the country first

You cannot create a country admin, a warehouse or a campaign for a country that has not been enabled here — it will not appear in the list to choose from.

Platform · Admins Super admin

Admins

The country administrator accounts. Super admin accounts are not managed from here.

Creating an admin

  1. Give their name and email address. Both must be unique across the platform.
  2. Optionally add a phone number.
  3. Choose the country they will run. This decides everything they can see.
  4. Set a password of at least eight characters and pass it to them securely.

The account is created Approved with its email already counted as verified, so they can sign in straight away.

Approved and pending

The Status column tells you whether an account can be used. An Approved admin can sign in and offers a Manage link. A Pending one cannot sign in and offers Approve instead.

Approve before you can edit

A pending account shows only Approve — there is no Manage link until it has been approved. To change a suspended admin's details, approve them first, then manage them.

Editing

Manage lets you change name, email, phone and country. Leave the password field blank to keep the existing password; fill it in to set a new one. The active switch suspends or restores console access — a suspended admin trying to sign in is told their account does not have admin access.

Changing someone's country

Moving an admin to a different country immediately changes every record they can see. Their old country's data becomes invisible to them.

Platform · Settings Super admin

Settings

Platform-wide configuration. The overview page shows what is set up and what is not.

Payments

Connects Pesapal so members can buy points from inside the app. Enter the credentials from your Pesapal account and Save settings, then:

  • Register IPN tells Pesapal where to report completed payments. Once done it reads Registered. Without this, payments succeed but points are never credited.
  • Test connection checks the credentials work before you rely on them.

Email & verification

The outgoing mail server. Until this is configured, no password resets or verification links can be sent. Enter the host, port, username, password, encryption, and the address and name mail should come from. The password is stored encrypted — leave it blank when editing to keep the one already saved.

Two tickboxes control who must confirm their address before they can sign in:

  • Require members (app users) to verify their email
  • Require admins to verify their email

Finish with Save settings. Then use Send test to post a message to your own address and confirm it arrives — save before testing, or you will be testing the previous settings.

Set up email before turning verification on

Switching on admin verification while SMTP is not working can lock every administrator out of the console — the link they need can never be delivered.

Sign-in methods

Enables "Continue with Google" in the mobile app. Paste in the client credentials from your Google project. Leave it unconfigured and members simply sign in with email and password.

Logo & favicon

The logo shown in the console sidebar and on the sign-in page, and the icon shown in the browser tab. Remove the logo and the console falls back to the Kugawana wordmark.

What members are told

Some console actions send a notification to the member's phone. Worth knowing before you click.

You do thisThey are told
Accept an order"Your request was accepted" — naming the food.
Accept a basket"Your basket request was accepted" — one message for the whole basket, not one per item.
Mark an order delivered"Order delivered" — naming the food.
Mark a basket delivered"Your basket order was marked as delivered."

Approving or rejecting a listing, granting points and cancelling an order change what the member sees in the app, but do not push a message to their phone.
